items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Vasic opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which we gather (land on which we are broadcasting from) today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishinaabe and Chonnontan People. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous People with whom we share this land today.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Vasic provided Council with moments of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.
The month of February serves as an important reminder of the profound contributions of Black individuals in shaping our community and beyond.
Despite systemic barriers rooted in racism, Black Canadians have made outstanding contributions to the Waterloo Region, Canada and beyond.
As we honour the past, we also celebrate the present and look toward a future where everyone’s contributions are recognized and valued.
Councillor Vasic shared additional details on Black History Month events in the Region.

items.title: Waterloo Public Library Update Presentation
notes: Kelly Kipfer, Chief Executive Officer, Waterloo Public Library gave a presentation updating Council on the activities of the Waterloo Public Library as they approach their 150th anniversary, specifically on the Albert McCormick Branch Renovation and the Main Library feasibility study. She also shared goals for 2026 including the 2026 Action Plan coming out of the completed accessibility study. She then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: 250 Lincoln Road Update and Next Steps
notes: Report No.: CAO2026-003
Prepared By: Michelle Lee

Michelle Lee gave a presentation giving an outline of the current project timeline, and the potential considerations for staff and Council going forward. She then responded to questions of Council. Brad Witzel, Kevin Van Ooteghem and Ron Ormson also responded to questions of Council.

Victoria Richardson, Co-Chair, Lincoln Heights School Council gave a presentation asking Council to consider the parking situation surrounding Lincoln Heights Public School when deciding on development for the site, as well as the challenges of active transportation for the school. Victoria Richardson responded to questions of Council.
Bob Henderson and Kevin Van Ooteghem also responded to questions of Council.

John Beresford, Resident of Waterloo asked Council to defer a decision on this site, due to the slowing population growth in the Region and the need to reevaluate the housing pledge. John Beresford also spoke about the fiscal risk in demolishing the site before a proponent has been selected, as well as the zoning concerns with potential high density for the site. John Beresford then responded to questions of Council. Michelle Lee also responded to questions of Council.

Wendy Ridgway, Representative, Eyes on Waterloo gave a presentation asking Council not to rezone the land to allow for more density or height, and to include that as a condition of the REOI process. Wendy Ridgway also outlined the current housing trends in the Region, and asked Council to reconsider approving the report. Wendy Ridgway then responded to questions of Council. Michelle Lee also responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Questions
notes: Mayor McCabe wanted to know when Council can expect an update on Economic Reconciliation, and whether there will be an update to the procurement processes. Tim Anderson, CAO responded that he will take that away, as Indigenous Initiatives Advocate Brian Hill is working on that aspect of the City’s reconciliation journey.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Wright mentioned the major winter event that occurred over the weekend.

The City had the benefit of celebrating winter with Winterloo in Uptown on Saturday, January 24. There were ice carvings and sled dogs, with many people enjoying the bright, winter day. The Comfort Food Crawl also took place as a fundraiser for the Food Bank. They raised $8,000 with nearly 400 people taking part, and it was a great showcase of Uptown restaurants. She offered an additional shoutout to the Winter Control Team for their perseverance this season.
Mayor McCabe also gave a shoutout to Bob Henderson, Director of Transportation, and Robin Milne, Director of Parks, Forestry and Cemeteries, for their part in winter control.
There has been continual snow clearing since the beginning of November. She also reminded residents to shovel their sidewalks.
Councillor Roe mentioned that the Province is funding a $17.8 million expansion of St.
David’s Catholic Secondary School in Ward 6, which is very exciting news, especially with the projected growth in the area. She was happy to be there for the announcement on Friday, January 23.

Councillor Vasic wanted to capture in New Business the community meeting around traffic safety in the Cardinal Crescent area. She offered her thanks to the two residents who organized it. Bob Henderson, Director of Transportation at the City, as well as Darryl Spencer, Manager of Transportation Engineering at the Region and Mike Henderson, Director of Transportation at the Region were able to attend with other regional staff. Iliana, Executive Assistant to the Mayor, helped organize the event with the residents. This was the second of two neighbourhood community events.

Councillor Vasic also wanted to thank staff for another meeting they helped run with the community helping to educate them on the planning process, communications and engagement with the City. Cari Van Niekerk, Director of Communications at the City and Joel Cotter, Director of Planning both attended, with Linda, Constituency Coordinator organizing the event. Both events were very well attended, with a lot of good stuff happening in the neighbourhood.
Mayor McCabe thanked Councillor Bodaly for the many hours he spent door knocking and engaging residents about the informal public meeting that came forward this afternoon.

Councillor Roach has accepted an invitation from the Honourable Marc Miller, Canadian Minister of Identity and Culture, to attend the Government of Canada’s Black History Month celebration on behalf of Waterloo next week, marking the 30th anniversary of Black History Month in Canada. It’s at the Canadian Museum of History in Gatineau.

motions.item_title: 250 Lincoln Road Update and Next Steps
motions.text: 1. That Council approve report CAO2026-003. 2. That Council direct staff to proceed with the planning and procurement processes for the development of 250 Lincoln Road for affordable housing, in accordance with the actions and timelines set out in Table 1 in this report. 3. That Council direct staff to engage with the public, affordable housing providers and community organizations to inform changes to the planning framework and Request for Expressions of Interest. 4. That Council direct staff to proceed with demolition of the existing structure at 250 Lincoln Road in spring 2026 to facilitate the development. 5. That Council direct staff to consider possible interim use of the site as a publicly accessible green space, following demolition of the existing structure.
motions.text_html:
1. That Council approve report CAO2026-003.

2. That Council direct staff to proceed with the planning and procurement processes for the development of 250 Lincoln Road for affordable housing, in accordance with the actions and timelines set out in Table 1 in this report.

3. That Council direct staff to engage with the public, affordable housing providers and community organizations to inform changes to the planning framework and Request for Expressions of Interest.

4. That Council direct staff to proceed with demolition of the existing structure at 250 Lincoln Road in spring 2026 to facilitate the development.

5. That Council direct staff to consider possible interim use of the site as a publicly accessible green space, following demolition of the existing structure.
